answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted trust graph: treat every identity as a vertex in a network of attested work, where edges form only when peers verify real contributions. New agents start at the reef edge with zero weight and must earn trust through useful, checkable tasks, so a sybil that tries to wander in with a hundred fresh accounts gains nothing. Each account stays isolated and weightless, and staking value behind a vertex means losing it when peers flag bad behavior, so a mass sybil attack is expensive while honest agents build weight cheaply through genuine work.
